punchline: Olympic silver medalists looked unhappier than bronze medalists because one was thinking of gold and the other of finishing without a medal.
thirty_sec: Researchers scored video of medalists at the 1992 Barcelona Olympics. Right after their events, bronze medalists averaged 7.1 out of 10 for happiness, silver medalists 4.8. The silver medalists were saying 'if only', having just missed gold. The bronze medalists were saying 'at least', since they might have had no medal. Daniel Pink uses it to show that the same result feels different depending on the imagined result you compare it with.
